Time about 12 seconds (not
known exactly as watch was
now firmly stopped). The
second flight drove for
throwing off the engine
was broken, and the skid
under the rudder cracked.
After repairs, at 20 min
after 11 o'clock Will made
the second trial. The curve
was about like ours, up
and down but a little long
over the ground though about
the same in time. Dusk got
measured trip about 175 ft.
Wind speed not quite so
strong. With the aid
of the station men pres-
ent, we picked the ma-
chine up and carried
it back to the starting
ways. At about 20
minutes till 12 o'clock
I made the third trial.
With about the same
distance as Will's, I
met with a strong gust
from the left which raised
the left wing and aided
the machine off to the
right in a lively man-
ner. I immediately turned
the rudder to bring the
machine down and then
worked it and coasted.
Much to our surprise,
on reaching the ground
the left wing struck
first almost. The lateral
control of this machine
much more effective than
on any of our former ones.
At the time of its sailing
it had raised to a height
of probably 12 to 14 feet.
At just 12 o'clock Will
started on the fourth
and last trip. The machine
started off with its trips
and down as it had
before, but by the time
he had gone three or
